text.en:
After the rain, a puddle lay in front of Kabir's house. By afternoon it was gone.
"Where did the water go?" he asked his mother.
"The warm sun turned it into vapour, and the vapour went into the air," she said.

Water exists in three states: solid (ice), liquid (water) and gas (water vapour).
When ice is heated it melts and becomes water. This is melting. When water is cooled enough it freezes into ice. This is freezing.
When water is heated it changes to water vapour. This is evaporation. It happens slowly even without boiling, and faster when it is hot, dry and windy.
When water vapour cools it changes back to tiny drops of water. This is condensation. Drops on the outside of a cold glass are condensed water vapour from the air.
Clouds, rain, rivers and the sea are linked in the water cycle.
Water has three states: solid ice, liquid water, and gas called vapour.
Heat ice and it melts into water. Cool water enough and it freezes into ice.
Warm water slowly turns into vapour. This is evaporation. Clothes dry in the sun because of it.
Cool vapour turns into tiny water drops. This is condensation. Look at a cold glass of water.

problem.en: Wet clothes dry faster on a hot, windy day than on a cool, still day. Why?

text.en: Wet clothes dry because the water in them evaporates.

why.en: Drying means water changing to vapour.

text.en: Heat and wind help evaporation happen faster.

why.en: Warm air gives energy and wind carries the vapour away.

text.en: So clothes dry faster on a hot, windy day.

prompt.en: A glass of cold water has drops on its outside. Where did these drops come from?

requiredIdeas.en: Water vapour in the air touched the cold glass.
It cooled and condensed into water drops.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking the water leaked through the glass.

points.en: Water can be solid, liquid or gas.
Melting: ice to water. Freezing: water to ice.
Evaporation: water to vapour. Condensation: vapour to water.
